notes:
T327 — score-annotated ASCII board (the human can now SEE the oracle while playing in Sabaki). The new weizigo_showscores GTP command renders two side-by-side boards: left = stones (existing showboard format), right = per-empty-point [L,H] for the side to move. Both boards row-align. GTP surface only: no solver, no artifact, no scoring change — only src/gtp.zig touched.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED (src/gtp.zig):
- Session.formatShowScores(side, out_buf) — a self-contained renderer. Renders header line, the two side-by-side boards (with row alignment), and a footnote that expands every L<H marker to its full bracket (axiom E3 — never fabricate a scalar from a bracket).
- weizigo_showscores [b|w] GTP command, added to KNOWN_COMMANDS (Sabaki feature-detects via list_commands). Default side = Black; explicit 'b' or 'w' picks the perspective. Reply is a multi-line block preceded by a leading newline (matches showboard's formatting).
- lookupChild helper: WZO2 path uses the (colex, -side, child_ko, passes=0) Markov key; WZO1 path uses (colex, -side) and treats UNDEF as a miss. Returns one of: legal_fixed (L==H, print the value), lh (L<H, marker cell + footnote), illegal (ko ban / suicide / PSK), miss (lookup miss — also prints a stderr line naming the state, same wording as bounds2).

CELL FORMAT (right board, 4 chars per cell, all right-aligned so digit positions column-align across the board):
  `  X ` / `  O `  — occupied cell (placeholder; not queried)
  ` +5 ` / `+16 ` / ` -5` — L == H, the value (Black-positive; sign always present so columns align)
  `+1~ `           — L <  H, sign + leading digit + `~` marker. For 2-digit |L| the cell shows sign + leading digit + `~` (e.g. L=-16 → `-1~ `); the full bracket still lives in the footnote, so no information is lost.
  `  . `           — empty point, illegal for the side to move (ko ban, PSK hit, suicide)
  ` ?? `           — empty point whose child is not in the artifact (lookup miss); also a stderr line naming the (colex, side, ko, passes) state, same wording as bounds2 — no silent fallback values, ever.

HEADER LINE: 'scores for B to move, +N = B ahead by N' (or W). The convention is Black-positive; the side argument picks the array, never the sign. The cell values are opponent-facing V0 at the child state (the same quantity `choose` compares), so a Black-move cell shows White's stored value for that child, and vice versa — but the header line states the convention once.

RENDERED SAMPLE (after 4 moves on 4x4, Black to move — this is a verbatim capture from the deployed binary with stderr suppressed):
  = 
  scores for B to move, +N = B ahead by N
  . . . .   -1~ -16 -16 -1~ 
  . X X .    +1   X   X  +1 
  . O O .   +1~   O   O +1~ 
  . . . .   -16 -1~ -1~ -16 
  marked (L<H): A4=[-16,-1], D4=[-16,-1], A2=[1,16], D2=[1,16], B1=[-16,1], C1=[-16,1]
  
The columns are right-aligned: `-1~` and `+16` line up at the rightmost content column, so the L<H marker (~) and the rightmost digit of the L==H value are in the same column. Stones (`X` / `O`) sit at the right edge of their 3-char content slot, in the same column as the rightmost content char of numeric cells.

WHY 'SILENT-UNLESS-ASKED': a per-move auto-print would interleave a multi-line block with Sabaki's GTP console on every play/genmove and bury the move reply. The board is a slow-readable artefact (you stop to look at it); the GTP loop is fast. The user calls `weizigo_showscores` whenever they want a fresh look, which is the natural Sabaki console pattern (query, then read). Recorded as a deliberate choice; the brief allows silent-unless-asked if explained.

CLAMPED vs UNCLAMPED: the brief floated clamping (-9 meaning ≤-9) as an option. Implemented the unclamped two-digit form first (the 4x4 max is ±16, fits in 2 digits). The brief says 'the human picks' after seeing samples — submitted the unclamped form with the rendered sample above. The clamped form would need a separate review and is out of scope for this task.

SIGN CONVENTION: every cell carries a sign so the column stays right-aligned with the sign of every value (e.g. `+16` not ` 16`, ` -5` not `-5`). The header line states 'B ahead by N' so the sign is unambiguous: positive = Black ahead.

REGRESSION TEST (inside gtp.zig, 'T327: weizigo_showscores — 2-digit value + illegal point + L<H point'): builds a minimal in-memory 4x4 WZO2 artifact (T283 pattern) with hand-crafted entries for a known mid-game position (B at B3/C3, W at B2/C2, Black to move), sets ko_point=2 to make C4 ko-illegal, and asserts the EXACT output block — a 2-digit value at A4 (+12), an illegal point at C4 (ko ban), and an L<H point at B4 ([1,5]). Golden string is a 5-line block (header + 4 board rows + footnote). Test passes.
